slots.jd.device-maker.about:
About us and the job
Copperline Devices is a small, owner-run company in Minneapolis that designs and builds medical devices. We are looking for a Hardware Engineer to help design, test and improve the boards inside our products. This is an on-site job. You will work at our bench alongside the people who build and support each device, and your work will go straight into products used by clinics and patients.
slots.jd.device-maker.duties:
What the job involves
- Plan, write and release firmware updates for the boards in our devices
- Write validation test plans and run them before each design goes to production
- Choose components with our suppliers, weighing cost, availability and quality
- Debug prototype boards on the bench and track faults to their cause
- Keep design records clear so others in the team can follow your work
slots.jd.device-maker.needs:
What you need
- 5 or more years of experience as a hardware engineer
- Hands-on skill in PCB layout for mixed-signal boards
- Working knowledge of Verilog and SPICE simulation
- Comfort writing Python scripts and working on Linux
- Experience using MATLAB for analysis of test data
slots.r1.b1: Leads design reviews for new boards and uses oscilloscope debugging to catch timing faults early, cutting rework after review by 30 percent.
slots.r1.b2: Writes Python scripts that package, flash and verify firmware updates across test boards, replacing manual update steps.
slots.r1.b3: Works with suppliers on component selection and checks candidate logic parts in Verilog simulation, reducing part qualification time by 50 percent.
slots.r1.b4: Builds validation test plans and writes Embedded C test routines that exercise each board function before release.
slots.r1.i1: Writes hardware specifications for new boards at Dunmore Technologies and turns them into designs that firmware and test teams can build on.
slots.r1.i2: Owns board bring-up at Dunmore Technologies, taking new hardware from first power-on to working firmware.
slots.r2.b1: Brought up new boards on Linux and wrote bring-up checklists that shortened first-boot time by 25 percent.
slots.r2.b2: Tested prototypes with JTAG debugging to trace faults to specific parts and firmware paths before design changes.
slots.r2.b3: Wrote board specifications with signal integrity requirements for high-speed traces, cutting late layout changes by 50 percent.
slots.r2.b4: Prepared PCB layout packages for design reviews and updated boards based on comments from senior engineers.
slots.r2.i1: Supported board bring-up at Meridian Cross, helping get new hardware powered, tested and running firmware.
slots.r2.i2: Worked with suppliers at Meridian Cross on component selection, comparing parts for cost, availability and fit with each board design.
slots.summary.1: Hardware and embedded engineer with about 5 years of experience owning a board workstream end to end, from PCB layout to firmware bring-up. Uses JTAG debugging and oscilloscope work to find faults and get boards ready for production.
slots.summary.2: Mid-level hardware engineer with about 5 years of experience taking one product line from schematic to tested board. Handles PCB layout, firmware bring-up and JTAG debugging, and writes Embedded C and Python to test and update the hardware.
